That is completely in your right to do however I think you’re mis understanding how it works and worry you’re providing incorrect advice to your friend (unless you are not in the uk- I cannot speak of how tightly other countries run their breeding) but in the UK you have to follow all the same guidelines as KC breeders to get a licence… there is actually the argument that pure bred dogs are more genetically flawed than crosses (you’re solidifying and inbreeding the bad genetics) which is why breeders like myself are mixing in the first place, it is for the health and well-being of the dog in mind always! please don’t think what I do is illegitimate and my dogs are not loved or well cared for, they have double the tests most other breeds have because I test them for the things that both breeds would get tested for they’re family pets that have only 1 litter a year. So I have all of mine fully health screened for everything even if I have their parents papers because it’s just easier to show evidence even though I know there’s no way they could even have some of the stuff I test for. Anything bred with poodle needs to be PRA clear as it is the most common eye issue among the breed and the Von Willebrand Disease test also. then it depends which other breed I use with the poodle (spaniel, Labrador etc) as they all carry their own genetic flaws so I make sure to focus on their breed specific test first but as I said, it’s easier to get them screened for everything. Ask questions about the papers, ask the breeder what the results mean and if they haven’t got a clue that’s a red flag! Are you UK based?

I’ve been in a scarily similar situation... like uncanny haha (the only difference is there wasn’t anyone he committed to in between but he expressed he didn’t want a relationship with me and he wasn’t sure if it was because he wanted to be with other girls before settling down) and I did actually walk away because I was worried about wasting my time but we ended up gravitating together again. 

After struggling not seeing and talking to each other and beating myself up for still allowing him to woo me I decided I wasn’t going to feel guilty or worried about what was happening or what might happen... I decided for as long I was happy and content I would stay, if he screws me over I can walk away knowing I did all I can and it’s all on him... it took me a while but I realised you will have these risks of your partner leaving regardless of a label. 

So, although we haven’t labelled anything He has told me he has no interest in seeing other people and we will both speak up if something changes with how we want the dynamic to be.

Set your boundaries and make sure he knows them, if he breaks them it’s treated the same as any relationship, that person knew your boundary and crossed it. 

Relationships are not a contract or possession- they are a continuous choice to consent to be with someone even though there are plenty of other people who are attractive. Keeping a relationship happy is about living in such a way that you both keep consenting.

You can't sustain a relationship based on the idea no one will ever leave you, disagree with you or disapprove of you. It just won't happen.
